newsitem.title: ROMANIA: SOCCER-DINAMO BUCHAREST HOPE TO MAKE UP FOR ICELAND DRUBBING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DINAMO BUCHAREST HOPE TO MAKE UP FOR ICELAND DRUBBING.

text.p: Top Romanian side Dinamo Bucharest have taken drastic measures in an attempt to make up for an embarrassing drubbing by a team of Icelandic amateurs and push through to the second preliminary round of the UEFA Cup.

Dinamo President Cornel Dinu has temporarily replaced coach Cornel Talnar for Wednesday's return match in Bucharest and promised to supervise preparations personally after last week's 2-0 away preliminary round loss to KR Reykjavik.
"Dinamo staff did not put the players in the right frame of mind for Reykjavik," Dinu told reporters after Dinamo's return from the capital of the country of fewer than 300,000 people.
"I will observe the training sessions myself and then decide which line-up to field."

Dinamo, twice European club competition semi-finalists in the 1980s, clearly suffered from overconfidence against the Icelandic side last week. Icelandic clubs have won only three of 23 matches in European club competitions since 1955.
The lowly Icelanders, only too happy to take advantage of their lapses, were predicting the two-goal lead would be enough to vault them through to the next round.
"We're in a good position and can enter the second match fairly relaxed," KR's coach Haraldur Haraldsson told the newspaper Morgunbladid.
"The pressure is on Dinamo and we'll need to play a disciplined game. We should get through to the next round but we'll need to play sensibly if we want that to happen."
Several KR players told the daily they were able to pick holes in what they described as Dinamo's largely predictable style.

"Dinamo started to read our game by the end of the match but that made no difference," Bjarni Thorsteinsson said. "Our weapon will be determination. They're quite soft and cry a lot. We must take advantage of that and go in for hard tackling."
Dinu was national team coach in 1992 and 1993 but was dismissed in the run-up to the 1994 World Cup campaign after Romania was defeated 5-2 by Czechoslovakia.
Dinamo's European history was tarnished by a previous first-round upset loss to Albania's 17 Nentori (now SK Tirana) which put them out of the 1986-87 Cup Winners' Cup.
"I'm optimistic even if some of our team's chances seem to be compromised," Dinu said. "Dinamo will go through."
